defs.def: the ability to do sth dangerous, or to face pain or opposition, without showing fear 勇气；勇敢；无畏；胆量

ex.s: Typically, cruelty and cheating are discouraged, while cooperation, humbleness and courage are praised.
ex.t: 通常，残忍和欺骗受到谴责，而合作、谦逊和勇气则受到赞扬。

ex.s: I joined a pre-presentation dinner with him and that smaller setting allowed me to slowly build up my courage to speak one-on-one with him—an idea that had seemed completely impossible.
ex.t: 我和他一起参加了一个讲座前的晚餐，那种较小的环境让我慢慢积蓄勇气与他一对一交谈——这曾经看似完全不可能。

ex.s: She built up her courage to speak up.
ex.t: 她建立起了发言的勇气。

ex.s: Write a poem about how courage, determination, and strength have helped you face challenges in your life.
ex.t: 写一首诗，讲述勇气、决心和力量如何帮助你面对人生中的挑战。

ex.s: "You needn't try it if you don't want to," Mum said, but I gathered all my courage to take a bite and was amazed to find it wasn't so bad.
ex.t: "如果你不想试，可以不试，"妈妈说，但我鼓足勇气咬了一口，惊讶地发现味道还不错。

ex.s: This insight grew from the determined attitude of a six-year-old boy who had the courage and perseverance to make his dream a reality.
ex.t: 这种领悟源于一个六岁男孩的坚定态度，他有勇气和毅力把自己的梦想变成现实。

ex.s: Patience, they say, is what I must now choose for my guide, and I have done so - I hope my courage will remain firm to continue until the bitter end.
ex.t: 他们说，现在我必须选择耐心做我的向导，我已经这么做了——希望我的勇气能坚定地支撑我，直到最艰难的最后。

ex.s: However, sending people there will require all the skill, courage and intelligence of the human race.
ex.t: 然而，送人去那里将需要人类全部的技能、勇气和智慧。

ex.s: Youth means a temperamental predominance of courage over timidity of the appetite, for adventure over the love of ease.
ex.t: 青春意味着勇气战胜胆怯的气质优势，冒险战胜安逸的爱好。
